title: Likelihood-free inference with nuisance parameters through normalizing flows
why_read: A technically interesting statistics method connecting normalizing flows to classical hypothesis testing, but niche and mainly of interest to statisticians rather than general engineers.
analysis: The paper proposes using normalizing flows, a type of neural generative model, to automatically discover near-pivotal test statistics for problems with nuisance parameters, without needing an analytic likelihood. It shows the approach can recover classical results like the one-sample t-test and outperform existing methods like the Welch test in certain regimes, while being faster than profile likelihood-ratio techniques. This is a solid piece of statistical methodology work bridging machine learning and classical inference, but its audience is fairly specialized in applied statistics or physics-style likelihood-free inference. General software engineers are unlikely to find direct application.
